findings.text: Upheld as advisory. The DESTINATIONS doc comment is separated from its declaration by the inserted REMOTE_ALIAS (questions 6 and 10). This is housekeeping and hides no behaviour.
Upheld as advisory. An orphan doc comment was left behind when counterOfEpoch moved to levels.ts (questions 4 and 10).
Upheld as advisory. policyWith is exported from production code with no importer in src/ or tests/ (question 8).
Upheld as advisory. The re-export of GENERATION_KEY and newGeneration only serves a test import (questions 5 and 8).

Upheld as advisory. The header says every caller that changes sharing goes through policyInForce, but the viewer's two PUT routes use loadPolicy plus sharingRefusal without the reconcile, so the change log can record a lost alias differently from the dock than from the CLI. ADR 0025 names only GET /api/sharing and share as reconcilers, so the code matches its contract and the comment overclaims. Narrow the comment or route the two PUTs through policyInForce.
Upheld as advisory. The variable `sent` holds every ledger record of kind entry, received ones included, so the name says less than it holds (question 3).

Upheld as advisory. The two sharing key strings are declared again in several server-side places beside SHARE_ROOTS and SHARE_AREAS in settings.ts (question 2). The viewer's copy in patch.ts has a stated reason.
Upheld as advisory. The restore toast reads '1 projects' with no singular, while the CLI's same sentence uses plural (question 6). Cosmetic.
Upheld as advisory. The optional RestoreOptions.dataDir falls back to resolvePaths().dataDir, which only tests use. The rubric calls this advisory because it hides no failure (question 9).
Upheld as advisory. This item adds ADR 0025, which makes the line 'ADR 0025, not written yet' stale (question 11). It is a documentation fix.

Upheld as advisory. AC-5's recorded text in criteria-round-three.md and the test disagree on a sent record of another version. The test matches the spec line in force (spec.md:333), and spec.md:346 records that the author's decision on the superseding criterion is pending. The test is not wrong against the spec. The recorded criterion text still needs the author's decision.
Upheld as advisory. Nothing checks the clause 'its other assertions unchanged' for module-migrations.test.ts against part 1's version. The new case has its own red run under AC-1.
Upheld as advisory. 'The hash only for candidates with a ledger record' is proven on the helpers, as the criterion allows. No wouldLeave-level test would fail if every candidate were hashed.
Upheld as advisory. 'Never the error's message' is checked only as the absence of the literal error.message. The pinned sentences still fail on reversion.
Upheld as advisory. install's legacy prompt is covered only through unit tests of askYesNo, never through install.ts's confirm.
Upheld as advisory. The warning is not asserted to name WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_SHARE_AREAS. The rest of AC-12's warning is pinned.
Upheld as advisory. The memory count cannot tell the store from the copy. The no-.replaced- check at line 386 still pins the criterion.

Upheld as advisory. OutgoingEntry.frontmatter carries the author's name, and ADR 0025 does not say the author leaves. Nothing is sent in this part, so no person's data leaves today. Part 6 must either state it in the ADR or pin the frontmatter fields that may leave.

Upheld as advisory. validatePatch now refuses CR and LF, which closes the round-one injection (probes/newline-in-a-setting.md). Refusing every C0 control would be extra hardening, and the reviewer shows no widening path without it.
Upheld as advisory. GET /api/sharing writes (reconcile, log, index refresh). It sits behind the global Host and token checks, so no new caller reaches it. This is a pattern note.
Lowered to advisory (debt). A restored store stays in rollback-journal mode. probes/restore-journal-mode.md shows this predates the item, and the first round's judge moved it to its own item.
Lowered to advisory (debt). The existing links toast still shows error.message. This item's own sharing toasts use fixed sentences.

Upheld as advisory. The projects line reads '1 projects share knowledge' with no singular (evidence: review/ui/settings-sharing-problems@1512.png, listed in review/ui/manifest.json). A copy slip, not a raw error or placeholder.

Upheld as advisory. The problems alert shows the loader's problem strings, lower-case and naming the variable (evidence: review/ui/settings-sharing-problems@1512.png). The spec asks for problems joined by ' · ', and the strings are neither an error message nor a path, so question 5's defect does not apply.

Upheld as advisory. The level pill sits inside the links cell instead of after it, so on a project with no links it reads under the LINKS header (evidence: review/ui/projects-row-pill-knowledge@1512.png). This differs from the spec's placement but does not fail AC-10's 'pill only above Nothing'. A layout note.

Lowered to advisory. The one console entry (review/ui/console-settings-sharing-error.json) is Chrome's own 'Failed to load resource … 500 … /api/settings'. It is the server's answer to the write failure the session induced on purpose by making the data directory read-only. A write failure is a server error, so the page cannot reach that state without the browser logging it. The page itself logs nothing and shows only the plain toast. Question 10 asks for a console clean of errors the page produces. The browser's record of the induced fault is the state's evidence, not an error of the change.

Upheld as advisory. The manifest's `observations` note ('1 entry' in the locked state) describes the first-round seed. The retaken capture (review/ui/settings-sharing-locked@1512.png) shows 0 and agrees with the policy. The manifest text is stale, not the page.

Advisory. The declared loading and saving states are listed under notCaptured as transient states under a second, not under a summary.missing (the manifest has no summary, and there is no review/ui-evidence.json). The rubric calls 'a loading state missing under a second' an advisory, and the texts are asserted in tests/unit/ui-sharing-copy.test.ts. Responsive, keyboard, axe, motion and vitals are Not answerable (no plan viewports, snapshots or axe files). That is recorded as a gap in the run and is not a finding a line names.

Upheld as advisory. The rollback is stated (spec.md:360), and the migration's lack of a down path has its reason. The narrower case is not covered: a 0.6.0 restore of a backup taken under this release brings back that copy's levels and generation with no restore row, so the levels are in force again on re-upgrade. Nothing leaves in this part, and the levels show in the viewer and in share status, so no risk-rubric defect applies (no unlimited irreversible write, no unstated dependency, no invisible failure). Parts 5 and 6 must not treat a stored generation as proof that no restore happened. Line 359 and ADR 0025's Rollback paragraph should name the case.
Lowered to advisory (debt). WAL is turned on only at creation, so a restored store stays in DELETE journal mode. This predates the item (probes/restore-journal-mode.md) and is already its own item.

Lowered to advisory (debt of part 1, item 2026-11-08-003). migrateModules runs on every openDb, and the sharing migration's plain CREATE TABLE would fail on a store that holds the tables without the module row. No state the product writes leads there. The reviewer's open question on the loader's 20 ms target is answered by probes/loader-latency.md: with 90 projects, loadPolicy p95 is 0.16 ms and policyInForce p95 is 0.56 ms.

Upheld as advisory. The viewer's sharing PUTs answer 409 on a closed policy, which ADR 0025's viewer bullet does not list. The behaviour matches the CLI and is safe. Add the 409 to the ADR so the later parts read one route contract.

Upheld as advisory. The doctor sharing check calls loadPolicy, which logs (mkdir plus append) on a failed load, against runChecks' 'changes nothing' contract. The spec asks the loader to log once, so this is a convention clash, not a crossed boundary.
Upheld as advisory. The sharing bullet leaves out hash.ts and migrations.ts from the module's file map.

Upheld as advisory. The viewer's Project.remote comment says 'a git remote', while the server contract is a host-led remote (isHostLedAlias). It is a comment mismatch, and the behaviour is pinned by tests/integration/ui-sharing.test.ts:295.
Lowered to advisory (debt of the sibling item 2026-11-09-001 and part 1). The knowledge and engine bullets still say knowledge is not in BUILT_IN and the module default is memory.

Upheld as advisory. The OR in ledgerRecords prevents use of the primary key, so wouldLeave scans the whole sharing_ledger. The ledger stays empty until part 6, which should add an index or split the query.

Upheld as advisory. No retention is stated for sharing_ledger or sharing_changes, and compact prunes neither. Neither table holds memory or entry text, so no personal data is left without a rule. The growth limit should be stated before part 6 writes the ledger.

Upheld as advisory. reconcileLevels runs a per-level lookup under BEGIN IMMEDIATE on every read of the policy. At most one row per project, and probes/loader-latency.md measures policyInForce at p95 0.56 ms over 90 projects.
Lowered to advisory (debt). WAL is set only at creation, so restored stores leave WAL. This predates the item (probes/restore-journal-mode.md).
Lowered to advisory (debt). entryAliases' case-insensitive LIKE cannot use the alias key, and the table is small.
